issue.title: Copy card C/L row previews middle-truncate away '● K on this page' and draw the dot gray, not accent

task_type_fields.impact: At the default card width the reader loses the page count that tells them whether C or L has something on the Highlights page they are reading; cosmetic, no payload is affected.
task_type_fields.location: bob-mac-capture Sources/RefsCore/RefsCopy.swift:149 (RefsCopyRow default .middle truncation; codeRow, linkPickerContentsRow) and Sources/BobMacCapture/Refs/RefsCopyCardView.swift:637 (plain Text(row.preview))
task_type_fields.repro:
Found by epic bob-cli-ct's land agent while reviewing bob-mac-capture CI render artifacts for run 40407215560 (commit 2764ec5). Evidence: `file:explicit:322b1400187c912a478f0c18` (refs-copy-card-link-rows-light.png).

In that render the card's catalog rows read:

- `5 blocks · ● 1 o…t, makefile, yaml`
- `9 links · ● 3 on…lopers.openai.com`

Both plans (`plan:202610/ref_code_block_copy.md` for C, `plan:202610/ref_link_copy.md` for L) specify `N … · ● K on this page · sites` with the dot in accent color. The mockups tail-truncate the site list.

Root cause:

- `RefsCopyRow.init` defaults `truncation: .middle` (Sources/RefsCore/RefsCopy.swift:149). Neither `codeRow` nor `linkPickerContentsRow` overrides it, so the middle elision drops the most useful part, "on this page".
- `RefsCopyCardView` draws `Text(row.preview)` as one plain run (Sources/BobMacCapture/Refs/RefsCopyCardView.swift:637), so the `●` never gets `Color.accentColor`. The picker rows (lines 193 and 381) do accent it.

Fix: give the C and L rows `.tail` truncation (or drop sites before page info), and render a leading `●` run in accent on those two rows. Then update the design fixtures and review the light and dark renders.

issue.creation_reason: Found while landing bob-cli-ct: the CI design render shows both catalog rows eliding the on-page count that both the C and L plans make the row's point, and the spec'd accent dot is gray.

payload.description: epic that added the L row inheriting the C row's preview rendering
